pr_body: #### What is it? - [ ] Bugfix (user facing) - [x] Feature (user facing) - [ ] Codebase improvement (dev facing) - [ ] Meta improvement to the project (dev facing) #### Description of the changes in your PR - **What the changes achieve:** for actions that require an Internet connection like, `Play here on background` and `Play here on Popup`, earlier a vague `Toast` message saying `Could not play this stream` would appear but a network connection is a common issue and it would've been helpful to know if that's what was wrong. So, these changes implement a `Snackbar` message for the same with an action to go to the `Downloads` section for offline viewing. - The changes add a `boolean requireNetwork` parameter to `StreamDialogEntry` that is `false` by default and can be changed via the `setRequireNetwork` method. If `true`, when the option is clicked on, before performing the action, network availability is checked, and if a network is unavailable, an indefinite `Snackbar` is shown. - I went with this approach since custom actions can be defined for a `StreamDialogEntry` and maybe more options might be added later that require network connectivity. They will be easier to integrate into these checks. #### Before/After Screenshots/Screen Record - Before: - After: #### Fixes the following issue(s) - Fixes ##6381 #### APK testing [debug.apk](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/suites/4071163970/artifacts/103515630) Also, apologies for taking so long :( I had exams. And sorry about the second commit :( I left an unused import in there somehow. #### Due diligence - [x] I read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
pr_comments: I don't understand. Why do you want the user to go to Downloads?

> I don't understand. Why do you want the user to go to Downloads?

Well, my thinking was that if a network is not available, maybe users could watch one of their downloaded videos. Youtube does something similar right?

Well, Youtube's downloads are playable in-app. Ours aren't. So the functionality doesn't actually match.

Personally, I would drop the link to Downloads. Maybe link to the error log instead? That could be helpful in providing bug reports related to network issues.

Anyway, I'll let a developer comment on this.

An error might be a little confusing to the users, suggesting there's a more serious issue maybe? 
Maybe a better action would be to automatically turn wifi/data on.

> Maybe a better action would be to automatically turn wifi/data on.

That will require adding an otherwise useless but dangerous permission. Just opening the Network and Internet menu would be good enough.

> An error might be a little confusing to the users, suggesting there's a more serious issue maybe?

We already have snackbars for non-serious errors, such as failing to fetch related videos. So I don't think we're doing anything drastic here.

> We already have snackbars for non-serious errors, such as failing to fetch related videos. So I don't think we're doing anything drastic here.

okay :) I'll add that then! Thanks!

> Maybe link to the error log instead? That could be helpful in providing bug reports related to network issues.

This should be done only if the error really comes from the player, but if I understand correctly this PR does not do that. If there is just an `if` before executing `StreamDialogEntry`'s code that checks for internet access, then there is obviously no real error to report, hence we should show no button at all.

I'm closing this since we went down a different path and added error notifications. Now the player correctly reports errors in a notification, and the enqueueing process also does, so this PR is not relevant anymore. Thank you anyway :-)

comments: Maybe we could check the internet connection at launch and then open a prompt to ask to either enable/check Wi-Fi connection or enable mobile data.

Hi. @skyGtm can I do this one? :)
And should it be a `Toast` or a `Snackbar`? Since other errors thrown by `Exoplayer` are also displaying `Toasts` maybe it'd be more consistent if this was a `Toast` as well?

>Maybe we could check the internet connection at launch and then open a prompt to ask to either enable/check Wi-Fi connection or enable mobile data.

I was thinking it would be better to let user know about his internet connection status only when he clicks links that require internet connection.
Unlike Official Youtube App, NewPipe is supposed to be distraction free, checking the internet connection at launch only triggers people to open the Internet Connection and get lost in the new feed like in official Youtube app.


> Hi. @skyGtm can I do this one? :)

@laksh-21 Yes you can proceed ahead. :smiley: 
But you don't have to ask me I am not a moderator. :smiley: 

Generally, if you see you can work on any issues just leave a comment "I am working on this issue" to let another potential contributor to know that you are working on this issue.
Above I see no other comments saying "I am working on this issue", I think you are good to work on this issue.

>And should it be a `Toast` or a `Snackbar`? 

I prefer 'Snackbar' because:
1. it can have infinite timeout (until user Turns ON internet connection)
2. user can dismiss it manually if user don't want to turn ON Wi-Fi or Mobile Data and just browse previously loaded feed, or he is just fiddling with settings.
3. It can have User actions to directly turn ON Wi-Fi or Mobile Data from the bottom of the screen. (without having to reach the top of the screen to open Quick Settings panel and then turn on Wi-Fi or Mobile Data.)

>  maybe it'd be more consistent if this was a `Toast` as well?

This is question for discussion.
@mhmdanas @SameenAhnaf @litetex @Stypox @opusforlife2

>I prefer 'Snackbar' because: Reason 1: I agree with you. YouTube app works this way. However, `Network Unavailable` and `Downloads` should be mentioned on the left and right side of the snackbar respectively. On YouTube app, the user is redirected to Downloads if no connection is found. However, it'll be nicer to let the user choose what to do. The user may want to check his connection and continue on the same page. Reason 2 & 3: I'm not sure what we'd like to do in this regard. I personally don't find it problematic. But some users may find it so. A. Considering Newpipe's privacy friendly design, some users might be skeptical on the regard of allowing Newpipe to turn on Wi-Fi and cellular connection. They might just want to stretch their hands instead. B. Many users like my grandparents may find it comfortable to pull down the notification panel instead of allowing hardly understood permissions. C. The snackbar might look too clunky. Many users love Newpipe's simple UI.

review_comments: Mmmh, we aren't doing this with all other `Snackbar`s across the app, why do it here?
Uhm, indefinite length is not a good idea, I'd just use `LENGTH_SHORT`, it doesn't take much time to read a snackbar that says "Network not available"
Note for a future PR: this method and all of the other methods related to `ConnectivityManager` distributed across the app should be moved into a separate `util.` class.
